text:
Adrian Kempe scored 36 goals last season. This year he has six in 21 games on 9.8 expected goals, and none in his last eight despite about 2.7 expected in that run. His 62 shots lead to good looks; they just aren't going in at his usual rate, under 10% against roughly 14% in a normal year.

The rest of the picture is strong. The Kings take about 57% of expected goals at five on five with him out there, far better than without him, and his teammates have scored about six fewer goals than their chances deserve on his shifts. Both of those numbers point to more points coming, not fewer.

The week had some noise: Kempe was fined for a high stick on Toronto's Dakota Joshua, the same night NDTV Sports noted he went from a controversial penalty to shootout hero. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season flagged both penalties and defense as costs. What to watch: the goals, and whether his line keeps winning the chance battle while they arrive.
headline: Kempe's chances deserve better
